  B)         Given a 128-bit block cipher and the key  
  $$K=0x2B7E151628AED2A6ABF7158809CF4F3C, compute the CMAC for the message$$  
  m=Hello. Assume padding is required to make the message length a multiple of the (5)  
  block size (128 bits). Show the steps involved in computing the MAC.  
  
  5)              Consider a one-time password system where the OTP is generated using a shared secret  
  key K=0xABCD1234 and a counter value of C=5. If the OTP is generated using  
  HMAC-SHA256, calculate the OTP for the counter value C=5. Show the intermediate (5)  
  A)         steps, including the result of the HMAC-SHA256 function.  
  
  B)         Scenario: A new online banking application has been developed that uses both data-  
  origin and entity authentication mechanisms to enhance security for its users. The  
  application employs one-time passwords (OTPs) and a challenge-response  
  authentication system to verify users.  
  
  i) Describe how the online banking application utilizes data-origin authentication and  
  entity authentication. What are the benefits of using both methods in this scenario?      (5)  
  ii) Suppose Alice wants to log in to her online banking account. She receives a challenge  
  in the form of a nonce from the server. Explain how the challenge-response protocol  
  works in this situation, detailing the steps Alice must take to authenticate herself  
  securely.
